claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation in FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers is governed by a transition between interface-mediated deformation mechanisms.
Dislocations initially accumulate at standard interfaces.
Dislocation accumulation at standard interfaces delays plastic flow.
Optimized crystallographic orientation and controlled interface segregants promote localized interface sliding.
CoCrFeMnNi or AlCoCrFeNi systems can serve as examples of the proposed FCC/BCC HEA multilayers.
Changing deposition parameters can modify crystallographic orientation, interfacial abruptness, and interface misorientation angles.
Minor Nb or Ti additions during deposition can produce localized interfacial segregation that alters bonding.
Interface geometry and chemical gradients modulate dislocation transmission.
Interface geometry and chemical gradients can activate interface sliding.
Tailored crystallographic structure and interfacial segregants decrease the energy barrier for dislocation transmission.
A decreased barrier for dislocation transmission facilitates a transition to localized interface sliding.
The combined alteration of dislocation dynamics and activation of interface sliding governs progressive plastic deformation.
Engineered multilayers will exhibit an initial delay in pronounced plastic flow.
Engineered multilayers will shift from dislocation pile-ups toward measurable interface-sliding events.
Enhanced local segregant concentrations at interfaces will correlate with changes in creep-rate profiles relative to baseline samples.
Baseline multilayers display typical dislocation accumulation across interfaces.
Baseline multilayers display uniform creep-rate behavior under the stated testing conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the nanoscale multilayer remains intact without substantial delamination or recrystallization.
Both dislocation dynamics and interface sliding are active in the approximate temperature range 300–400 K.
Preliminary evidence supports significant effects of interfaces on deformation in high-entropy alloys.
